chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I wrote to him asking him about the slave upon whom death is presented, so the master emancipates him at that moment, so he exits the world as a free man. Is there for his master a reward in that, or should he leave him so that there is for him his reward when he dies and he is a slave? So he wrote to him: 'Leave the slave as a slave in the state of his death, so it is a reward for his master, and this emancipation at this time is not beneficial for him.'

key_terms.يَحْضُرُهُ الْمَوْتُ: Death is presented to him / at the hour of death

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for a master who frees his slave at the moment of death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies the spiritual efficacy of *manumission in the final hour* (‘itq fi al-sa‘a), ruling that keeping the slave enslaved until death yields greater reward for the master than emancipating him at the moment of death. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that late-stage manumission lacks the enduring merit of earlier, more substantial acts of charity, as the slave’s status changes only at the threshold of the afterlife. The ruling underscores the principle that the timing and context of charitable acts significantly influence their spiritual weight in Shia legal tradition.
